recipes.name: Peanut Butter Vegetable Chicken Soup
ingredients_raw: salt and ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Bring broth, chicken, potatoes, and carrots to a boil in a large stockpot over medium-high heat. Reduce the heat to medium and cook until vegetables are tender, about 10 minutes. Stir in zucchini, broccoli, tomatoes, celery, onion, bell pepper, and garlic; simmer until tender, about 8 minutes.
Add peanut butter, parsley, salt, and pepper; stir until peanut butter is fully blended. Simmer for 3 more minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Peanut Butter Vegetable Chicken Soup
raw_recipe.description: This filling peanut butter soup made with leftover chicken, potatoes, and lots of vegetables may be the best soup you've ever tasted.

review.reviewBody: I made this soup the other night.I thought that the flavor was very good. after reading some of the reviews,saying that they thought it was very bland, I did change 1 thing about the recipe.Not the ingredients,but just one step.I began with 2 TBLES. olive oil,heated,added celery,onion, garlic,a little salt &pepper to that and sauteed them til soft.Then added the broth and the rest of the ingredient's.This usually adds more flavor to the broth.

Awesome! I must admit, I was skeptical about the peanut butter, but you must try it! I doubled all the vegetables, and the result was a very thick & hearty soup! I also used a rotisserie chicken, and added it to the very end, as it doesn't need to cook. I've never heard of a soup recipe not starting with oil and the onion, so I tweaked it: I heated 1 1/2 Tbl. olive oil, and added the celery, onion, bell pepper, and garlic, sauteeing until all were soft. I then followed the rest of the steps (as a timesaver, I used a can of *diced* tomatoes instead of whole). Note that using reduced fat peanut butter is just fine! I added 1/2 tsp. salt + 1/2 tsp. pepper at the end, and would use those measurements again. Thanks so much for the recipe!

The soup as listed is pretty good, but it can be excellent with some changes. I doubled all the veggies (tripling the garlic) and used a bit more chicken (2lb raw). I cooked the chicken in a crockpot with the tomatoes, a little salt and pepper, 1/2 tsp each granulated garlic, turmeric, and cumin, and 1/2 tbsp each chili powder and dried parsley; the blend spent 5 hours on low, then I shredded the chicken. I flash sauteed the onions, garlic and celery in 1/2 tbsp of olive oil and added the veggies, stock and chicken/tomato/spice mixture. I brought the pot to a boil, reduced the heat to medium, simmered for about 5 minutes, then added the peanut butter and fresh parsley. I let it simmer for another 15 minutes or so, leaving the lid on because the additional veg/chicken meant that I had to conserve as much liquid as possible. It was thick like a stew, and very flavorful. In terms of the appearance, the added spices gave the broth some very pretty red and orange notes. I'm giving the recipe only 4 stars as written, but I think it's worthy of 5 stars with my changes.

Just make it! Best soup I've ever eaten, and a huge hit with my friends! I use the "Fast Chicken Soup Base" recipe from Pam Anderson, and I love trying it with different vegetables, especially kale. After I served this to my friends a couple of times, they started adding peanut butter to other soups I made. 

To cut the sugar, I used 1/2 regular peanut butter, and 1/2 sugar-free and salt-free peanut butter from the grocery store (I set a tea strainer with peanut butter into the pot to prevent small pieces of peanut from getting into the soup). Definitely mix peanut butter into a separate pot with some broth first, then add to the whole pot of soup.

We REALLY liked this soup! My bf said it eats more like a STEW! HEARTY MEAL. I left out zucchini, but added cauliflower and mushrooms. I sauteed the onion, green pepper, celery, garlic, and 4 sliced mushrooms in 2Tbsp butter. When serving, I added a few dashes each of curry powder and ginger powder to bottom of each bowl. Man, did those additions enhance an already GREAT recipe. Thanks, Annie!

Since we like spicy I added 1 teaspoon of red pepper flakes to the soup and at the end of cooking time a tablespoon of fresh thai basil. I also used crunchy peanut butter am loved the texture it added to the dish. Terrific recipe and wonderful way to sneak lots of veggies into a meal.

So incredibly delicious! I followed the advice of another reviewer and added the peanut butter to a small amount of broth in a small saucepan, then added the peanut butter broth to the whole pot of soup. Great with yellow squash and kale, too! Just add kale closer to the end, and it turns a lovely green color as it cooks.

Really good. Based on the other reviews, I was worried the soup would be a little bland, so I sauteed the celery, onion, carrot and garlic in olive oil first with thyme and marjoram, and some red pepper flakes for a little kick. Then I added some mushrooms about two minutes before I added the chicken and potatoes. I used some mini potatoes I had left over and left the skins on for more nutrition. Then I added a can of corn with the zucchini, and I used a can of diced fire roasted tomatoes instead of the whole tomatoes. Not a big fan of green pepper so I left that out. I also used chunky peanut butter. When I tasted it, it was still missing a little something for me, so I added a little hot Hungarian paprika (I like spicy). Yum! I like that there was a lot of broth, but if you aren't a fan of broth I think about 6 cups chicken broth would be fine.

awsome soup!
I boiled the 2lbs of drum sticks in 8cups of water with 4 chicken bullion cubes. Once the chicken was cooked I took them out and cut them in to cubes then returned to the pot and continued the recipe as instructed. Everyone loved it from my 1 year old daughter to my 30 year old sister and our mother. Will definatly make this much more!

Wonderful! The best way to do this is definitely to boil a half chicken with skin on with a couple of carrots, celery, peppercorn, bayleaves for about an hour. Allow to cool and remove the skin and bones - use this as the cooked chicken. Use the stock from veggies & boiled chicken as your 8 cups and finish off with canned broth. I added tabasco at the end because I like a little kick to my soup. Such a wonderfully savory soup - my four year old threw a fit because he didn't want to eat dinner but couldn't help eating it all which means it's a winner in my house!

I love soup! I had alot of fresh broccoli and decided to try this recipe. There were a few vegetables that I left out. I browned the chicken first then put everything in the crockpot. I cooked it on high for 3 hours. I also added some brown rice on a whim the last 30 minutes. If you like spice, add some red pepper flakes and asian chile sauce. I can't wait to eat this again tomorrow! You won't notice the peanut butter!

I make this soup every winter and freeze in portion sizes. I use 1 cup of crunchy peanut butter; double the vegetables, add 2 cans of Rotel diced tomatoes; 1 Fire roasted tomatoes with green chiles, 1 diced tomatoes with habaneros. I omit the zucchini and substitute frozen sliced okra. The spiciness of the tomatoes and the peanut butter compliment one another nicely.

This is a fabulous soup recipe! It was originally published in Jane Brody's Good Food book. The only change I see here is a reduction in the amount of peanut butter from 1 cup down to 1/2 cup. I think this is why some people find it bland. Use the full cup and add lots of fresh ground pepper. You won't be disappointed!

I used the ingredients I had. I used frozen vegetables. Broccoli , cauliflower, carrots, squash, onions and garlic. Used a small can of tomato paste and a handful of fresh tomatoes. Added ground ginger, curry powder to the recipe. Used the Mediterranean chicken skewers from Costco as the chicken. It took a lot longer to cook those vegetables and get them soft but it was worth the wait. It was delicious

I often have leftover chicken and so thought this was a great find! I had all the ingredients on hand. I used half Campbell's chicken broth and half Campbell's Thai Pho chicken broth. I also added some fresh beans from our garden. We had it tonight and will definitely make it again!
I didn't have any broccoli but it turned out wonderful. If I make it again I might add a little grated fresh ginger to give it a kick. This recipe is a keeper!
This was good but I couldn’t tell the difference from other similar recipes. Not sure what the peanut butter does and I couldn’t taste it. Maybe I didn’t add enough?

I made this recipe but I pretty much doubled all the vegetable ingredients. For the 8 cups of broth, it was too watery for my taste. Other than that I followed the recipe as stated. My thanks to the original poster, for it was delicious!
My husband and I love this soup. The only change I’ve made was to omit the zucchini. Have made it at least 3 times and will make it again and again. It’s a real keeper!
It is very good!!!!
